editorial_note: GitHub listed sixteen projects this Saturday morning, the same sixteen as on Friday, and twelve of them were featured here in the past seven days. Today's three picks are all first-time cards: ==Intel's OpenVINO inference toolkit==, the AFFiNE notes-and-whiteboard workspace, and Ghost Downloader, a multi-protocol desktop download manager. projects.description: Intel's open-source inference toolkit: it ==converts and optimizes trained models== from PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, PaddlePaddle and JAX and runs them on CPUs, Intel GPUs and Intel NPUs, with C++, Python, C and Node.js APIs.
projects.why_interesting: It is a mature way to run vision, speech and language models on ordinary laptops and edge boxes without a CUDA card, and the separate ==GenAI API targets LLM pipelines==. The latest release, 2026.4.1 of 1 October, broadens LLM attention support in the ONNX frontend and hardens model and compiled-blob import against malformed inputs.
projects.caveat: Its accelerator paths are ==tuned for Intel hardware==: GPU and NPU support means Intel integrated and discrete GPUs and Intel NPUs, and the release notes list NPU crashes with certain Intel driver versions. Speed-ups are the maintainers' claims; measure them on your own models.

projects.description: A local-first workspace for notes and whiteboards: ==docs, canvas and databases share one editor==, so any block can sit on an edgeless canvas, and it can be self-hosted as an alternative to Notion and Miro.
projects.why_interesting: Your data stays on your own disk first, with real-time sync and collaboration on web and desktop clients, and the self-host guide lets a team keep the whole workspace on its own server. Few open tools merge long-form documents and a free-form whiteboard this closely.
projects.caveat: The licence is split: the client is MIT, but the ==backend server carries an Enterprise Edition licence== that ties production use to AFFiNE's subscription terms. The AI features are a hosted AFFiNE service, recent builds are canary and beta tags, and the last stable release, v0.27.4, dates from 18 August.

projects.description: A cross-platform desktop download manager: one app handles ==HTTP, BitTorrent, FTP, M3U8 and DASH streams==, with a browser extension that hands page media to the app and a ghd command line for scripted downloads.
projects.why_interesting: It runs on Windows, macOS, Linux and Android, offers an aria2-compatible RPC API for other tools, and lets you change a download's URL, headers or proxy mid-transfer without losing progress. The 4.5.11 release of 20 November added German, French, Indonesian, Italian and Korean translations.
projects.caveat: The README advertises ==real-browser TLS fingerprints to slip past anti-bot checks== and opens with a paid residential-proxy sponsor, and its YouTube and Bilibili support can conflict with those sites' terms and with copyright; download only what you have the right to. The maintainer says updates will slow down.
